newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK retail sales, M4 data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK retail sales, M4 data.

text.p: Following is a selection of reactions to UK retail sales, which were up 0.4 pct in October (vs expected +0.5 pct) and 4.1 percent y/y and October M4 money supply which was up a s/a 10.3 pct yy (vs expected 9.7 pct).
"While the UK retail sales were broadly in line with expectations, the money supply figures were much stronger than expected and will increase the pressure on the Chancellor to hike interest rates."

"Most of the gain in sales came in the clothing and footwear category which will have been affected by the turn to slightly colder weather. M4 rose 1.1 percent in October, much more than had been expected. This took the year/year rate up to 10.3 percent, well above the government's reference range. The lending figure was particularly strong at 7.4 billion stg. Though this may be distorted by the repo market, it will provide some concern to those who regard broad money as the best measure of future inflation."

"UK retail sales data pretty much in line with expectations. The usual suspects were strong -- clothing and footwear and household goods. Yearly trends also look pretty robust, with the economy set for a good Christmas period. It's pretty much as-you-were in relation to pressures on interest rates."

"UK retail sales figures are very much as expected, but the money supply figures are much more worrying. The lending figure of 7-1/2 billion should have been above expectations...the pressure to raise interest rates before the election will certainly increase on these figures."
